liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Morning Dew** (3 reviews): Dew is rare: the fourth of 1980, first since 11/8/79, and sixth in over three years; this version is gentle; Reviewer finds Morning Dew pretty great, the point where the show picks up after seeming on autopilot [13][16][19]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (1 review): Scarlet-Fire here is called incredible, like the one on 11-30 at the Fox Theater [14]
- **Fire On The Mountain** (1 review): The Scarlet>Fire jam is spacey and long [13]
- **Estimated Prophet** (1 review): The Estimated>Terrapin sequence is singled out as outstanding [21]
- **U.S. Blues** (1 review): Reviewer calls this the hottest U.S. Blues ever, and finds Set II great overall [19]

## The recordings

- **gd1980-10-14.155412.sbd.miller.flac24** (recommended): soundboard; 35 songs; 255 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [1]
- **gd1980-10-14.155439.sbd.1gen.miller.t.flac16**: soundboard; 35 songs; 255 min [2]
- **gd1980-10-14.156399.mtx.photoleon.t-flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 35 songs; 256 min [3]
- **gd80-10-14.sbd-aud.gardner.3828.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 35 songs; 234 min; rated 3.81/5 by 32 [4]. Said about its sound: The soundboard-audience matrix sounds crisp, though the acoustic set was not yet heard by this reviewer; Acoustic set sounds poor, but the second and third set soundboard has excellent levels and almost no hiss; Acoustic set sounds tinny, while the electric sets shine [12][21][23]

## Around the show

- Attendee on the 15th night of the Warfield run had a front-row ticket; Bill Graham decorated the theater impressively [18]
- Reviewer notes Garcia's guitar and emotion stand out, and the band lets songs flow without rushing [23]
- Final night of a 15-show Warfield run, with pre-birthday wishes for Bobby, turning 33 on the 16th [3]
- Reviewer's favorite electric Warfield set available, a companion to Dead Set; rivals the 11-30 Fox Theater show as 1980 pick [14]
- Setlist looks outrageous for 1980, a year of little variety, but reviewer finds the band on autopilot until Dew [16]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1980-10-14.155412.sbd.miller.flac24**: transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  January 18, 2017; source: SBD > Cassette Master (Nakamichi 550) > Cassette (Sony TC-D5M/TDK SA-C90) [1]. Also: Patch source for this FLAC24 soundboard came from Rob Eaton; pitch correction settings came from Joe B. Jones [1]
- **gd1980-10-14.155439.sbd.1gen.miller.t.flac16**: transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  January 18, 2022; source: SBD > Cassette Master (Nakamichi 550) > Cassette (Sony TC-D5M/TDK SA-C90) [2]. Also: This is a 16-bit conversion of the 24-bit 96kHz Miller soundboard; Rob Eaton supplied patches, Joe B. Jones pitch settings [2]
- **gd1980-10-14.156399.mtx.photoleon.t-flac16**: source: Matrix created in Adobe Audition by Joe Noel February 14, 2022 [3]. Also: Mix of two sources: one pitch-corrected and paused between songs, with fades smoothing transitions; Source flaws: a three-second dropout in Monkey and the Engineer, and Heaven Help the Fool lacks its first three seconds [3]
- **gd80-10-14.sbd-aud.gardner.3828.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard and Audience composite [4]. Also: Tracking seems made for 74-minute discs, so the first electric set's last two songs spill onto disc 3; The last two tunes come from a different source than the rest of the recording [12][20]

## Art and photos

- Poster by iCollector.com Online Auctions: [1980 Grateful Dead Warfield Theater Concert Poster](https://www.icollector.com/1980-Grateful-Dead-Warfield-Theater-Concert-Poster_i8463742) [25]
- Poster by Worthpoint: [Vintage 1980 Grateful Dead Warfield Theatre Poster | #29179909](https://www.worthpoint.com/worthopedia/vintage-1980-grateful-dead-warfield-theatre) [26]
- Poster by Dennis Larkins: [Grateful Dead Warfield San Francisco 1980 Poster](https://www.icollector.com/Grateful-Dead-Warfield-San-Francisco-1980-Poster_i24608842) [27]
